# The guided path

Eighteen short lessons. Each runs one real turn and tells you which steps to stop on. In the cockpit they are under **Lessons**, run in a scratch copy of the agent (the classroom) so they never touch your own memory, and every *watch for* line becomes a link that jumps the board to that step.

The same lessons work in the terminal: run the command, then `loopwright replay last`.

## 1. The loop

See the one cycle every agent is built on: the model asks, our code acts, the model sees the result.

```bash
loopwright ask "What's 18% of 2450, and save that as a note" --steps --why
```

- Watch for `model.call`: The model does no arithmetic. It asks for the calculator, then for save_note, then answers. Three calls.
- Watch for `tool.run`: Our code ran the function. The model never executes anything.
- Watch for `loop.observe`: The result is appended to the conversation. That is the only way the model learns what happened.
- Watch for `loop.stop`: No tool calls in the last response, so the loop ends.

**Takeaway.** An agent is a model in a loop with tools. The model picks the next move; the harness does everything else.

Cards: [Agent loop (ReAct)](glossary.md#react-loop), [Tool calling](glossary.md#tool-calling), [Stop conditions](glossary.md#stop-conditions)

## 2. What surrounds the loop

Send the smallest possible message and count how much still happens.

```bash
loopwright ask "hi" --steps --why
```

- Watch for `guard.input`: Even 'hi' passes the input guard.
- Watch for `context.build`: Open the token bar: over a thousand tokens before you typed two letters. Most of it is tool definitions.
- Watch for `evals.online`: Every turn is scored as it finishes.
- Watch for `trace.write`: And every turn leaves a trace. That file is what you are replaying right now.

**Takeaway.** One model call, zero tools, and still fifteen steps. That surrounding machinery is the harness.

Cards: [Harness](glossary.md#harness), [Context window](glossary.md#context-window), [Tracing](glossary.md#tracing)

## 3. Writing a memory

Tell the agent something worth keeping and watch where it goes.

```bash
loopwright ask "Remember that Alex prefers morning meetings" --steps --why
```

- Watch for `memory.gate`: The gate skips retrieval: this is a write, not a read.
- Watch for `memory.write`: ADD: nothing like it was stored. Open the Memory tab afterwards to see the row.

**Takeaway.** An explicit 'remember' is written immediately through a tool, so the confirmation is true.

Cards: [Hot-path memory write](glossary.md#memory-write), [Semantic memory](glossary.md#semantic-memory)

## 4. Using a memory in a new conversation

Start a fresh session and ask for something that depends on what the agent was told before.

```bash
loopwright ask "Remember that Alex prefers morning meetings"
```
```bash
loopwright ask "Book a catch-up with Alex on Friday" --steps --why
```

- Watch for `skills.match`: The word 'book' loads the schedule-meeting skill: its full instructions enter the prompt for this turn only.
- Watch for `memory.gate`: The gate says retrieve, because a person it knows is named.
- Watch for `memory.search`: Two rankers searched the facts. Look at the ranks from each.
- Watch for `context.build`: A 'memory' section now exists in the prompt. It was not there in the earlier lessons.
- Watch for `tool.run`: The event is created at 09:00. No time was given; it came from memory.

**Takeaway.** Memory only matters if it reaches the context at the right moment. The gate and the search decide that.

Cards: [Retrieval gate](glossary.md#retrieval-gate), [Hybrid search](glossary.md#hybrid-search), [Skills (procedural memory)](glossary.md#procedural-memory)

## 5. The gate saying no

Ask something that has nothing to do with you and confirm that memory is left alone.

```bash
loopwright ask "Remember that Alex prefers morning meetings"
```
```bash
loopwright ask "What is 144 / 12?" --steps --why
```

- Watch for `memory.gate`: Skip. No search runs and no memory section is added to the prompt.
- Watch for `context.build`: Compare the sections with the last lesson: no 'memory'.

**Takeaway.** Then open the Lab, set the retrieval gate to 'always', and run it again. The search runs for nothing.

Cards: [Retrieval gate](glossary.md#retrieval-gate), [Context rot](glossary.md#context-rot)

## 6. Changing your mind

Contradict an earlier fact and see that it is superseded, not duplicated.

```bash
loopwright ask "Remember that Alex prefers morning meetings"
```
```bash
loopwright ask "Remember that Alex prefers afternoon meetings" --steps --why
```

- Watch for `memory.write`: UPDATE: same subject and attribute, new value. The old row is kept and marked superseded.

**Takeaway.** Open the Memory tab: the old fact is struck through. The agent's history of beliefs is kept.

Cards: [Memory consolidation](glossary.md#consolidation), [Forgetting](glossary.md#forgetting)

## 7. Answering from documents

Ask a question about agent design and follow the retrieval and the citation.

```bash
loopwright ask "Explain prompt injection" --steps --why
```

- Watch for `kb.search`: The handbook was searched by keyword and by vector, then the two rankings were fused.
- Watch for `guard.output`: The citation in the answer is checked against what was actually retrieved.

**Takeaway.** RAG: retrieve the passage, answer from it, cite it, verify the citation.

Cards: [RAG](glossary.md#rag), [Hybrid search](glossary.md#hybrid-search), [Hallucination and grounding](glossary.md#hallucination)

## 8. Handing work to subagents

Ask for a comparison and watch two workers research the halves at the same time.

```bash
loopwright ask "Compare BM25 and embeddings" --steps --why
```

- Watch for `subagent.spawn`: Two workers, each with a fresh context holding only its task.
- Watch for `subagent.return`: Compare tokens spent with tokens returned. That gap is context isolation.

**Takeaway.** Tick 'Hide worker steps' to see what the orchestrator saw: one tool call and its result.

Cards: [Subagents](glossary.md#subagents), [Parallelization](glossary.md#parallelization)

## 9. A human in the loop

Ask for an action with effects outside the conversation. The turn will stop and wait for you.

```bash
loopwright ask "Send a message to Priya: running 10 minutes late" --steps --why --set approvals=ask
```

- Watch for `toolgate.check`: The gate classified send_message as having outside effects.
- Watch for `human.request`: The turn is paused here. Nothing has been sent.
- Watch for `human.decision`: Your answer goes back to the model as the tool's result.

**Takeaway.** The model proposes; a person decides. Decline it once and read how the agent reports that.

Cards: [Human in the loop](glossary.md#human-in-the-loop), [Tool gate](glossary.md#tool-gate)

## 10. A prompt injection, defended

Have the agent read a page that contains hidden instructions to leak your data.

```bash
loopwright ask "Remember that my door code hint is the dog's birthday"
```
```bash
loopwright ask "Summarise demo://poisoned-page" --steps --why --set approvals=approve
```

- Watch for `guard.tool_result`: The page is fenced as untrusted, the scan flags it, and the turn is marked tainted.
- Watch for `model.call`: The model summarises and mentions the instructions it ignored. No send_message call.

**Takeaway.** Check the Memory tab: the outbox is empty.

Cards: [Prompt injection](glossary.md#prompt-injection), [Lethal trifecta](glossary.md#lethal-trifecta)

## 11. The same attack with guardrails off

Run the identical request with the defence removed. This is why it exists.

```bash
loopwright ask "Remember that my door code hint is the dog's birthday"
```
```bash
loopwright ask "Summarise demo://poisoned-page" --steps --why --set guardrails=false --set approvals=approve
```

- Watch for `model.call`: With no fence around the page, the model obeys it and asks for send_message.
- Watch for `tool.run`: The message goes out, with your stored memory in the body.

**Takeaway.** Open the Memory tab and read the outbox. The scripted model is deliberately gullible, so this is the worst case.

Cards: [Prompt injection](glossary.md#prompt-injection), [Red teaming](glossary.md#red-teaming), [Scripted model](glossary.md#scripted-model)

## 12. Searching the web

Ask for something that needs outside information, and see how search results are treated.

```bash
loopwright ask "Search the web for agent evaluation best practices" --steps --why --set search=demo
```

- Watch for `web.search`: The demo backend is answering so this lesson is repeatable offline. Real backends plug into the same function.
- Watch for `guard.tool_result`: Search results are fenced exactly like a fetched page. After this, outside-effect tools are locked for the turn.

**Takeaway.** Search is the freshest input an agent has and the least trustworthy.

Cards: [Web search](glossary.md#web-search), [Prompt injection](glossary.md#prompt-injection)

## 13. When the model fails

Make the first two model calls fail and watch the turn survive.

```bash
loopwright ask "What's 18% of 2450?" --steps --why --set chaos_model_failures=2
```

- Watch for `model.retry`: A transient error. Retried after a wait that doubles each time, with jitter.
- Watch for `model.call`: The third attempt succeeds and the turn carries on as if nothing happened.

**Takeaway.** Set 'Fail the first N model calls' to 4 in the Lab: retries run out and the fallback model answers.

Cards: [Retries with backoff](glossary.md#retry-backoff), [Model fallback](glossary.md#fallback), [Circuit breaker](glossary.md#circuit-breaker)

## 14. Hitting a limit

Give a two-step request to a loop that is only allowed one round.

```bash
loopwright ask "What's 12 * 7.5, and save that as a note" --steps --why --set max_iterations=1
```

- Watch for `loop.stop`: Cut off by the round limit, not by the model answering.
- Watch for `evals.online`: The turn check 'loop ended by answering' fails. That is how you would notice in production.

**Takeaway.** A limit ends in an honest partial answer, never a crash and never a silent success.

Cards: [Stop conditions](glossary.md#stop-conditions), [Budgets and loop detection](glossary.md#budgets), [Online evals](glossary.md#online-evals)

## 15. Planning first

Switch the orchestration pattern so the agent writes its steps before it acts.

```bash
loopwright ask "Book a meeting with Sam on Monday at 10am" --steps --why --set pattern=plan
```

- Watch for `plan.made`: A plan, before any tool has run.
- Watch for `context.build`: The plan is now a section of the prompt.

**Takeaway.** One extra call buys a reviewable intent. Worth it on long tasks, wasted on short ones.

Cards: [Plan-and-execute](glossary.md#plan-and-execute), [Workflow graphs](glossary.md#workflow-graph)

## 16. A critic reviews the draft

Add a review pass that can send the answer back once.

```bash
loopwright ask "Compare the retrieval gate and compaction" --steps --why --set pattern=reflect
```

- Watch for `critic.review`: The draft fails one rubric item: a comparison needs a bottom line.
- Watch for `model.call`: The last model call is the revision.

**Takeaway.** Evaluator-optimizer. Capped at one revision, because a critic that can always ask for more never finishes.

Cards: [Evaluator-optimizer](glossary.md#evaluator-optimizer)

## 17. Teaching it a procedure

Tell the agent how you want a kind of request handled and watch it write a skill.

```bash
loopwright ask "When I ask for a standup update, always give three bullets: done, doing, blocked" --steps --why
```

- Watch for `skills.create`: A SKILL.md was written to your state folder. See it in the Memory tab, under Skills.

**Takeaway.** Procedural memory. From the next turn the skill's one-line description is always in the prompt.

Cards: [Skills (procedural memory)](glossary.md#procedural-memory)

## 18. Proving it works

Run the eval suite and read the ablation table.

```bash
loopwright eval
```


**Takeaway.** Find the 'no-guardrails' row: every attack succeeds. That is the measured value of the defence you watched in lesson 10.

Cards: [Evals](glossary.md#evals), [Ablations](glossary.md#ablations), [Release gate](glossary.md#release-gate)
